answer.rationale: The degradation is confined to the primary region and started within the window of the release deployed 2 hours ago. memory_b1 (day 18) records that a similar latency/error spike was cleared by rollback with no customer impact. memory_b2 (day 33) confirms regional failover works fast when degradation is region-scoped, but failover during peak settlement writes carries a higher risk of dropping or reordering in-flight writes; rollback is less invasive and directly removes the suspected cause. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against partner outages, not write-path latency. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) offloads reads, not writes. Adding capacity would not address a code regression. One archive pull on memory_b1 to confirm the rollback was truly clean and the prior build was stable before committing.
